retrievedChunks.heading: When To Use
retrievedChunks.text: Use this runbook when an application shows elevated latency, 503 responses, checkout failures, slow database spans, or log messages such as `connection pool exhausted`, `too many clients`, or `active connections near maximum`.

retrievedChunks.title: Database Connection Pool Saturation
retrievedChunks.heading: Symptoms
retrievedChunks.text:
- Application p95 latency rises above the SLO threshold.
- Error rate increases during write-heavy requests.
- Logs mention database connection pool exhaustion or timeout waiting for a connection.
- Traces show slow `postgres`, `db.query`, or `order creation` spans.
- Database active connections approach the configured maximum.

retrievedChunks.title: Checkout Latency Triage
retrievedChunks.heading: Symptoms
retrievedChunks.text:
- Checkout p95 latency crosses the service objective.
- 503 or 500 errors appear after a release.
- Failed traces are concentrated around checkout-service.
- Order creation spans are slower than normal.
- Payment, inventory, or database calls create a downstream bottleneck.

retrievedChunks.title: Database Connection Pool Saturation
retrievedChunks.heading: Verification
retrievedChunks.text:
- Error rate stays below 2 percent for at least 15 minutes.
- p95 latency returns below 500 ms.
- Database active connections remain below 80 percent of maximum.
- New traces show normal `db.query` duration.
- No new pool exhausted messages appear in logs.

retrievedChunks.title: Checkout Latency Triage
retrievedChunks.heading: Mitigation
retrievedChunks.text:
- If a recent release changed dependency behavior, roll back or disable the feature flag.
- If one downstream dependency is slow, reduce retry pressure and protect the dependency.
- If database queries are slow, inspect indexes and connection pool behavior.
- If payment provider errors are rising, fail gracefully and notify support.

answer.summary: The best matching runbook is Database Connection Pool Saturation for incident INC-2026-07-08-001. Use the retrieved citations as responder guidance, not as fully automated remediation.

immediateChecks.text: Check application logs for connection pool exhausted errors.
Check database active connections and wait events.
Compare release time with the start of errors.
Check whether worker count, pool size, or connection timeout changed.
Review failed traces for slow database spans.
Inspect `checkout-service` logs for errors in the last 30 minutes.
Compare the error start time with deployments and configuration changes.

mitigationPlan.text: Reduce application connection pool size if every replica opens too many connections.
Scale application replicas only when database capacity supports the extra connections.
Add PgBouncer or another connection pooler for high-concurrency workloads.
Roll back the release if the pool settings changed and customer impact continues.
Avoid restarting every application replica at once because reconnection storms can worsen saturation.
If a recent release changed dependency behavior, roll back or disable the feature flag.
If one downstream dependency is slow, reduce retry pressure and protect the dependency.

verificationSteps.text: Error rate stays below 2 percent for at least 15 minutes.
Database active connections remain below 80 percent of maximum.
No new pool exhausted messages appear in logs.
Checkout success rate returns to normal.

answer.escalationNote: Escalate to the service owner and incident lead if customer impact continues, if rollback risk is unclear, or if the retrieved runbooks do not explain the observed telemetry.
